My idea is to build a low cost screening tool: a clip-on lens for a normal smartphone camera that takes a photo of the retina, and a small neural network that runs on the phone itself, with no internet, to flag likely glaucoma. Health workers in primary clinics would use it during routine visits and refer only the flagged people to an eye hospital. I want to know whether something like this has already been published, and what is closest to it.
